newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to endorse proposed ban on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to endorse proposed ban on human cloning.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday will endorse a U.S. ethics commission's recommendation that Congress enact legislation to ban the cloning of entire human beings, the White House said.

The National Bioethics Advisory Commission on Saturday proposed that scientists or doctors may make cloned human embryos for research purposes but proposed prohibiting implanting them into women's wombs to make viable babies.
Clinton was scheduled to receive the commission's report at 11:45 a.m. EDT (1545 GMT) in the White House Rose Garden.

"The general thrust of that (report) was proposed federal legislation that would ban human cloning," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. "He (the president) agrees with that recomendation and he will say so at 11:45."

Clinton asked the panel in February to review the complex legal and ethical ramifications of cloning after scientists in Scotland reported they had cloned a lamb -- which they named Dolly -- from a single cell taken from an adult sheep.
Their success was controversial, raising the prospect that the procedure could be used to make humans genetically identical to an existing man or woman.

The advisory commission of 18 scientists, lawyers and theologians sought to reconcile the views of opponents of cloning who regard it as an affront to nature and demand a complete ban, and supporters who see it as a stunning scientific breakthrough with promising medical repercussions.
Polls taken shortly after the announcement of the cloning of Dolly showed 90 percent of Americans opposed human cloning.
